source.title: The Map Behind the Flow: Finite-Step Gradient Descent as a Dynamical System

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Analyzes finite-step gradient descent in exactly solvable scalar, factorized, and linear-network models and reports explicit dynamical outcomes, but does not test benchmark classification error under the recipes in the versions.
record.gate_note: Rows record the paper's own model results relevant to training dynamics. It does not measure CIFAR training classification error or test the stated random-initialization benchmark recipes; benchmark-error versions are therefore not tested. Cited results from prior work are excluded.
record.test_reason: The paper derives and simulates finite-step recovery from an initially unstable representation in a squared-loss linear neural chain (R10). Section 6.1 also analyzes full-batch linear-network dynamics in which leading-mode curvature oscillates across the stability threshold while other modes continue learning. These bear on V5 through theoretical models. Depth scaling alone does not test V3, and representation selection does not test V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that finite-step dynamics can sustain organized post-edge oscillation and drive balancing, alignment, and representation selection in solvable models. They explicitly leave progressive sharpening unexplained and distinguish these models from realistic network training.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes fixed-step gradient descent in analytic scalar, factorized, and aligned linear models; it does not use the benchmark recipes or classification-error measure in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Step size relative to stability edges; depth and its learning-rate scaling; singular-value spread and frame misalignment; activation; persistent target noise; finite-depth outer escape scale.

fits_no_version.finding: Scalar quartic and depth-scaled quotient maps exhibit stable cycles, period doubling, chaos, and separate escape scales.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For these scalar losses, crossing a fixed-point stability edge can produce bounded periodic or chaotic dynamics before escape.

fits_no_version.finding: Finite steps and persistent target noise contract factor imbalance; noise produces a crossover in the transverse balancing exponent.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Residual fluctuations can select balanced factorizations in minimal linear models.

fits_no_version.finding: Spectral spread controls frame stability and the rate of convergence to post-edge attractors; data coupling adds alignment dynamics.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Post-edge orbit stability and attraction rates depend on spectral separation and alignment in linear factorizations.

fits_no_version.finding: Activation shape determines stable valley representations and permits terminal ReLU inactivation at large steps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learning rate can select accessible representations or cause unit inactivation in single-neuron models.

record.problems: The paper uses highly simplified analytic models rather than benchmark classifiers. Several dynamical phase boundaries and exponents are based on numerical calculations or simulation; the authors identify an averaged near-edge approximation and note that a full analytic proof of transverse-exponent negativity is absent.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for space. The study's benchmark classification-error results are absent; cited results by other authors were not entered as rows.

untested.parts: CIFAR training classification error, random or corrupted labels, random initialization, model-size effects, early stopping, and regularization.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student local-minimum frequencies and the benefit of one or two extra student neurons.
Depth-related training-error degradation in plain batch-normalized convolutional networks; identity shortcuts; very deep plain tanh training; Fixup.
Comparisons of activation-matched initialization schemes, signal or gradient propagation, orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization, and initialization-dependent training speed or trainable depth.

Recovery in wide randomly initialized networks relative to their initial linearized-model threshold; empirical progressive sharpening over long training; general divergence boundaries in those networks; divergence from starts below the initial threshold. The tested recovery uses a minimal linear chain and a local Hessian threshold.
Batch normalization versus no normalization, higher tolerated learning rates under batch normalization, and Fixup comparisons.

missing.what: Record the joint training behavior of different singular modes: transient curvature growth, leading-mode oscillation across 2/a, continued convergence of other modes, and the stated possibility of continued loss decrease. Preserve the aligned-manifold assumption and distinguish this from progressive sharpening.

record.verdict_notes: Residual in this paper generally means prediction residual, not an identity residual shortcut. No V3 or V4 test follows from the paper's discussion of depth or representations. Nonzero periodic-orbit loss and absence of divergence in a scalar limiting map do not independently challenge V5's stated network results.

versions.untested_parts: Benchmark training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, model size, random initialization, and effects of early stopping or regularization.
Teacher-student two-layer ReLU problems, spurious local minima frequency as widths grow, and the effect of student width exceeding teacher width.

The paper examines depth and residual behavior in scalar and deep linear models, not the version's plain versus residual batch-normalized convolutional benchmark networks or their training errors. It also does not test the cited special-initialization and Fixup results.

It studies depth-scaled finite-step dynamics and aligned deep linear modes, but does not compare activation-matched initializations, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, or trainability across initialization schemes.

It studies post-edge learning-rate dynamics in analytic models, but does not test wide-network squared-loss recovery above the initial linearized stability limit, full-batch neural-network sharpness hovering, or the cited divergence cases.
No batch-normalization versus no-normalization comparison or Fixup recipe evaluation.

rows.subject: quartic gradient map ga(x) = x − ax(x² − 1)
rows.operation_detail: Vary learning rate a and analyze fixed point and post-edge cycles of the scalar gradient map.
rows.measure: Convergence of iterates to a minimum; one-step loss monotonicity.
rows.value: For 0 < a < 1 the minima attract every initial point in the stated basin; loss decreases monotonically throughout that basin for 0 < a ≤ 2(√2 − 1) = 0.828427 . . . .
rows.note: Analytic scalar toy loss, not classification error or a benchmark network.
rows.check: Scalar-loss convergence and monotonicity do not measure any version's specified network behavior.

rows.subject: quartic gradient map ga(x) = x − ax(x² − 1)
rows.operation_detail: Increase learning rate beyond the fixed-point stability edge and derive period-two orbit stability.
rows.measure: Stability of the period-two orbit born at a = 1.
rows.value: The period-two orbit is attracting exactly for 1 < a < √5 − 1.
rows.note: Exact result for the scalar quartic map.
rows.check: Attraction to a scalar two-cycle does not establish neural-network loss recovery, curvature reduction, or continued learning.

rows.subject: quartic gradient map ga(x) = x − ax(x² − 1)
rows.operation_detail: Increase learning rate through successive period-doubling thresholds.

conditions.value: a > 1; cascade thresholds reported through a32

rows.measure: Attracting periodic-orbit sequence and cascade accumulation.
rows.value: fixed point → two-cycle → period-doubling cascade → chaotic finite-step dynamics; a∞ = 1.3022834 . . . .
rows.note: The paper says later thresholds are solved numerically.
rows.check: A scalar bifurcation cascade does not measure the behavior specified by V3 or V5.

rows.subject: depth-n scalar chain ℓn(x) = (x^(2n) − 1)²/(4n)
rows.operation_detail: Scale learning rate as a = c/n and take the large-depth limit of the quotient gradient map.
rows.measure: Convergence of quotient dynamics to a limiting map and fixed-point stability edge.
rows.value: hc,n converges uniformly on compact subsets to hc(u) = u exp{2c u(1 − u)}; fixed point u = 1 is locally stable for 0 < c < 1.
rows.uncertainty: Uniform O(1/n) error on compact subsets is stated.
rows.note: The study is theoretical and concerns a scalar chain.
rows.check: A quotient-map limit and local stability threshold do not measure depth degradation, shortcut benefits, or recovery during training.

rows.subject: Ricker-type depth-limit quotient map hc(u) = u exp{2c u(1 − u)}
rows.operation_detail: Vary scaled learning rate c and solve for the attracting two-cycle and its flip threshold.
rows.baseline: fixed point loses stability at c = 1
rows.value: The limiting map has an attracting two-cycle for 1 < c < c1.
rows.check: Stability of a limiting scalar two-cycle does not establish the training behavior named by V5.

rows.subject: Ricker-type depth-limit quotient map hc(u) = u exp{2c u(1 − u)}
rows.operation_detail: Vary scaled learning rate c across the cascade accumulation point.
rows.value: Post-cascade dynamics has chaotic invariant sets interspersed with periodic windows; no finite-c divergent phase occurs in the depth-limit dynamics.
rows.note: The finite-depth escape mechanism is said to occur on a separate outer scale.
rows.check: Boundedness in a scalar depth limit neither tests the specified network recovery nor contradicts divergence at larger rates in wide networks.

rows.subject: finite-depth quotient maps hc,n
rows.operation_detail: Vary c at finite depth and characterize the fixed-point flip and subsequent attracting dynamics.
rows.measure: Fixed-point flip, period-doubling cascade, and post-cascade dynamics.
rows.value: The fixed point flips at c = 1; numerically the finite-depth picture has two-cycle loss of stability near c1, cascade accumulation near c∞, and chaotic intervals interrupted by periodic windows.
rows.uncertainty: Later thresholds described as numerically consistent; not stated
rows.note: Finite-depth quotient dynamics, not benchmark error.
rows.check: Finite-depth scalar bifurcations do not measure plain versus residual network training error or V5's recovery trajectory.

rows.subject: finite-depth scalar chain ℓn(x) = (x^(2n) − 1)²/(4n)
rows.operation_detail: Analyze escape under the outer-scale quotient update.
rows.baseline: u = O(1) depth-limit dynamics has no finite-c divergence
rows.value: Escape occurs on the scale u ≍ √(n/c); uesc = √(2n/c)(1 + O(n^(−1/2))).
rows.note: Reports finite-depth escape away from the universal inner scale.
rows.check: An outer-scale scalar escape boundary is not a measured network training outcome. The displayed asymptotic concerns large n at fixed c, rather than an exact boundary formula at arbitrary finite depth.

rows.subject: two-factor gradient descent map (x+, y+) = (x − ary, y − arx)
rows.operation_detail: Vary step size a and determine normal stability of the solution valley xy = 1.
rows.baseline: balanced point is at the flip threshold for a = 1
rows.value: The normally stable arc is |Δ| < Δ*(a), with Δ*(a) = (2/a)√(1 − a²); for a > 1 no point on the valley is normally stable.
rows.note: Toy factorization model; not a classifier.
rows.check: Normal stability of valley points supplies a threshold but does not itself show recovery, a loss burst, or sharpness hovering.

rows.subject: two-factor gradient descent map (x+, y+) = (x − ary, y − arx)
rows.operation_detail: Run finite-step gradient descent from a valley point beyond its normally stable arc and analyze the residual burst and selected endpoint.

conditions.value: ε0 > 0 just beyond the normally stable arc; near-edge scaling ε = O(μa)

rows.measure: Residual oscillation, imbalance, and endpoint sharpness.
rows.baseline: unstable-side starting point above the edge
rows.value: Residual grows and oscillates, contracts imbalance, and the burst returns to the stable arc at ε∞ ∈ (−μa/4, 0); endpoint is short of balance in the stated near-edge regime.
rows.uncertainty: Averaged near-edge approximation; endpoint error O(μa²) as stated.
rows.note: The paper explicitly calls the selection law an averaged near-edge approximation.
rows.check: Remove V3. The start must have a small nonzero residual seed near an unstable valley point; an exact zero-residual valley point remains fixed. The recovery and endpoint law concern the stated near-edge regime, and the law is an averaged approximation.

rows.subject: two-factor gradient descent map on invariant diagonal x = y
rows.operation_detail: Vary step size a and determine transverse stability of the diagonal period-two orbit.
rows.measure: Transverse multiplier and Lyapunov exponent of diagonal post-edge dynamics.
rows.baseline: diagonal scalar period-two orbit is attracting for 1 < a < √5 − 1
rows.value: The period-two transverse multiplier is 3 − 2a and is attracting for 1 < a < 2; numerically χ⊥ < 0 for 1 < a < 2 and approaches zero at a = 2.
rows.uncertainty: The sign over the interval is numerical evidence; complete analytic proof is not provided.
rows.note: Transverse stability is distinct from training classification error.
rows.check: Transverse contraction toward a diagonal attractor measures factor balancing, not V5's loss recovery or sharpness trajectory. Transverse stability also does not imply longitudinal stability of the two-cycle.

rows.subject: aligned two-mode depth-two linear network
rows.operation_detail: Vary step size and singular-value spread to determine stability to frame misalignment.
rows.measure: Local stability of aligned post-edge two-cycle against physical frame misalignment.
rows.value: Locally stable if and only if a(s1 + s2) < 2; beyond this rotational edge misalignment grows with precession, and numerically the full system saturates in a persistently misaligned oscillatory state with nonzero loss.
rows.uncertainty: The saturation description is numerical; not stated
rows.note: The result identifies a condition where the aligned reduction fails and loss remains nonzero.
rows.check: Frame-misalignment stability and an unquantified nonzero oscillatory loss do not establish failure to attain low loss or failure of sharpness hovering. They do not test V3.

rows.subject: two-mode depth-two linear network
rows.operation_detail: Optimize a single learning rate over two modes as singular-value spread varies.
rows.measure: Minimax per-step contraction factor and optimal learning rate.
rows.baseline: best sub-edge contraction at σ = 1/2 is 0.333
rows.value: For σ < 0.5718 . . . the minimax rate lies beyond the top edge; at σ = 1/2, a*s1 ≈ 1.120 gives contraction about 0.120 per step.
rows.uncertainty: Threshold and example are numerical approximations; not stated
rows.note: An optimization-rate result in a two-mode linear model.
rows.check: The contraction factor measures approach to a fixed point or periodic orbit, rather than reduction of training loss to a minimum. Faster convergence to a two-cycle is not itself V5's recovery.

rows.subject: aligned deep linear network with L factors
rows.operation_detail: Analyze balanced mode-wise stability edges as network depth and target singular values vary.
rows.measure: Normal sharpness and local stability edge for each mode.
rows.value: Balanced mode i has normal sharpness L si^(2−2/L) and edge ai = 2/[L si^(2−2/L)]; largest singular mode crosses first.
rows.note: Analytic result on an aligned invariant manifold.
rows.check: The local sharpness and stability-edge formula alone does not record the evolving curvature and loss behavior described separately in Section 6.1.

rows.subject: data-coupled two-factor model ℓ(x,y) = 1/2 ||xy − d||²
rows.operation_detail: Vary normalized step A = a||d|| and analyze aligned balanced period-two orbit and its multipliers.
rows.measure: Orbit stability, balancing, and alignment multipliers.
rows.baseline: flattest zero-loss solution reaches the edge at A = 1
rows.value: An exactly aligned and balanced period-two orbit exists and is linearly stable; multipliers are μcyc = 9 − 2(1 + A)², μbal = 3 − 2A, and μalign = 1 − A with multiplicity k − 1.
rows.note: Minimal data-coupled model; no classification benchmark.
rows.check: Linear stability of an aligned, balanced periodic orbit measures orbit attraction, alignment, and balancing; it does not establish the loss-recovery trajectory specified by V5.

rows.subject: one neuron with linear readout and tanh activation
rows.size_stated: one activation and one linear readout
rows.operation_detail: Vary step size a and identify which zero-loss valley representations are stable.
rows.measure: Stability of saturated solutions and finite flat valley window.
rows.value: For a < 2, saturated solutions remain stable; for 2 < a < 1 + √2 only the flat window is stable; for a > 1 + √2 no valley point is stable.
rows.check: Stable representation windows do not measure initialization effects or actual recovery of loss during training.

rows.subject: ReLU neuron with linear readout on balanced diagonal
rows.operation_detail: Vary step size around the critical-image threshold for entering the absorbing inactive half-line.
rows.measure: Forward invariance of active well and possibility of terminal inactivation.
rows.value: For a ≤ a*, the positive well is forward invariant; for a > a*, active trajectories can enter the absorbing half-line and crossings are terminal.
rows.uncertainty: Typical-orbit absorption beyond threshold is numerical; not stated
rows.note: The threshold is exact on the balanced diagonal; typical-orbit behavior is described numerically.
rows.check: Large-step inactivation of a single ReLU unit is distinct from the wide-network recovery and divergence regimes specified by V5.

rows.subject: two-factor model with noisy target ℓt(x,y) = 1/2 (xy − 1 − ξt)²
rows.operation_detail: Add persistent Gaussian target noise and estimate sub-edge transverse balancing exponent.

conditions.value: ξt iid N(0, σ²), sufficiently small σ

rows.value: χ(a,σ) = −a²σ²/(1−a) + O(σ⁴); for sufficiently small target noise the balanced diagonal is transversely attracting throughout the sub-edge range.
rows.note: Persistent label noise is a model assumption; not minibatch noise.
rows.check: The transverse balancing exponent under persistent target noise measures a different outcome from V5's deterministic loss and sharpness behavior.

rows.subject: two-factor model with noisy target ℓt(x,y) = 1/2 (xy − 1 − ξt)²
rows.operation_detail: Simulate the noisy map and compare the measured transverse exponent with the edge-crossover normal-form prediction.
rows.measure: Measured-to-predicted exponent ratio nearest the edge.
rows.baseline: normal-form prediction ratio 1 in the σ → 0 limit
rows.value: Ratios are 1.35, 1.13, 1.05, and 0.99, respectively, converging to one as σ → 0.
rows.uncertainty: Finite-σ effect stated; no error bars reported.
rows.note: The text reports validation values for the noisy-map prediction, not classification performance.
rows.check: This validates a balancing-exponent approximation rather than any claim version. The noise-to-ratio pairing is wrong: ratios 1.35, 1.13, 1.05, 0.99 correspond respectively to sigma 0.08, 0.05, 0.03, 0.01.

relationships.condition: Two-factor squared-loss linear chain, 0 < a < 1, initialized near an unstable valley representation with a small residual seed in the near-edge regime.
relationships.reason: R10 shows a growing oscillatory residual reducing imbalance and sharpness until the trajectory returns below the stability threshold and the residual dies out.
relationships.display_finding: A growing oscillatory residual reduced imbalance and sharpness until the trajectory returned below the stability threshold and the residual decayed.

relationships.condition: Aligned deep linear networks with separated singular modes under full-batch gradient descent.
relationships.reason: Section 6.1 describes leading-mode curvature crossing and oscillating around 2/a while other modes converge and loss can continue decreasing; this is text-based evidence missing from R14.
relationships.display_finding: Leading-mode curvature crossed and oscillated around 2/a while other modes converged and loss could continue decreasing.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
